Astonishingly, this came following a four-match losing streak, with three of those coming in the opening three games of the campaign.

Six of those have come in the Premier League era. We look back over each of those unbeaten runs. web.description: When you think of "unbeaten" and "Premier League", your thoughts might immediately be drawn to Arsenal's incredible title-winning campaign in 2003-04.
snippets: When you think of "unbeaten" and "Premier League", your thoughts might immediately be drawn to Arsenal's incredible title-winning campaign in 2003-04. The Gunners went an amazing 49 games without falling to defeat that season, leading them to clinch the Premier League title. They are the only side to have ever won the Premier League without falling to defeat once – hence the "Invincibles" title – and though their streak is the longest in the top-flight, other records have come close.

Expectations were high for Pep Guardiola's 2017-18 Manchester City side, who seemed to steamroll over just about everyone – until they paid a visit to Liverpool in January and shockingly lost 4-3, ending their dreams of an unbeaten run (they had a streak of 30 games). City ended up winning the league that season with 100 points, but not without two defeats (to Liverpool and Man Utd). Chelsea, under Jose Mourinho, managed a 40-game unbeaten run through October 2005, followed by Arsenal's 30 matches through October 2002. Liverpool became just the fourth team to record 30 straight unbeaten games in the Premier League following their victory over Crystal Palace in November 2019, in a run that started after their loss against Manchester City in January 2019.

Following their comeback 2-1 win at Wolverhampton Wanderers, Manchester City are now on the outright fourth longest unbeaten run by a team in Premier League history. Man City have now gone 31 matches without losing in the competition, dating back to their 1-0 defeat at Aston Villa in December 2023.

Man City would need to go another 18 matches unbeaten to equal Arsenal's Premier League record of 49 games in a row without defeat, a run that stretched over three seasons, including their 2003/04 "Invincibles" campaign. City are 10 away from going outright third on the all-time list and surpassing Chelsea's run of 40 matches unbeaten.
